extracted.intended_audience: stand-up comedians, comedy writers, and storytellers studying personal-story comedy craft
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for writing and performing personal-story (memoir-as-material) stand-up bits in a three-act narrative form, emphasizing honesty, callbacks, and emotional resonance alongside jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Personal-Story Doctrine
rubrics_metrics.description: Birbiglia's signature is comedic story (memoir as material). His craft talks emphasize narrative structure as the spine on which jokes hang.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use personal, memoir-style material as the basis for comedy; prioritize a coherent narrative spine and treat jokes as ornaments that must serve the story rather than distract from it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-act spine for a story bit (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Birbiglia Three-Act for a Story Bit: Act 1 setup (~25%), Act 2 complication (~50%), Act 3 resolution (~25%). The jokes inside each act must serve the act's purpose — laughs that break the story are CUT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the bit so the audience follows a trajectory from normalcy to escalation to a resolution that surprises emotionally and comically; remove jokes that derail the narrative even if they get laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act 1: Normal, recognizable setup
rubrics_metrics.description: Act 1: A normal, recognizable setup. We are in your world. (~25%)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish the everyday situation and the comic's perspective quickly and concretely so the audience knows where the story starts; keep it roughly a quarter of the bit's length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act 2: Complication and escalation
rubrics_metrics.description: Act 2: A complication that escalates. We are following a trajectory. (~50%)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop the conflict or problem and escalate stakes or absurdity over the bulk of the bit, maintaining forward momentum and building toward an emotional/comedic payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act 3: Surprise resolution (emotional + comic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Act 3: A resolution that surprises us emotionally AND comically. (~25%)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Close the narrative arc with a payoff that resolves the trajectory and delivers both an emotional insight and a comedic twist; aim for closure rather than an open-ended punch.

rubrics_metrics.name: "What I Should Have Done" reveal
rubrics_metrics.description: Birbiglia frequently structures the punchline as: 'And I should have realized X. But I was 22, so instead I...' This signals to the audience that the comic understands the absurdity NOW, which gives them permission to laugh AT past-self.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use retrospective self-awareness as a device: show current understanding (comic-now) contrasted with past behavior (comic-then) to invite compassionate laughter and to signal growth or recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cold open with specific image
rubrics_metrics.description: Open with a small, specific image (a brown paper bag, a hospital bracelet). The image reappears in act 3 as a callback that closes the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with a concrete, evocative detail that can be later used as a callback to close the loop; audiences enjoy the closure of a repeated image tying beginning and end together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty as the engine
rubrics_metrics.description: "If it's not embarrassing, it's not interesting." The story must reveal something the comic would rather hide. The audience laughs because they recognize the same shame in themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be willing to reveal true embarrassment or vulnerability; authenticity and shame-based recognition drive emotional resonance and comic payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working Rubric: clear three-act spine
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a clear three-act spine?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether the bit has a discernible setup, escalation, and resolution; absence of a spine suggests restructuring is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working Rubric: opening image that closes in act 3
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there an opening image that closes in act 3?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify a concrete image or detail introduced early reappears as a callback in the resolution to provide closure and thematic unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working Rubric: comic-now makes peace with comic-then
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comic-now make peace with comic-then?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the performer demonstrates present-day understanding or acceptance of past actions, allowing the audience to laugh at the past-self without cruelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working Rubric: all jokes serve the story
rubrics_metrics.description: Are all jokes in service of the story (none that break it)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminate funny bits that are tangential or interrupt narrative momentum; prioritize jokes that advance character, escalate the situation, or reinforce themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working Rubric: willingness to be embarrassed
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the comic willing to be embarrassed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the material includes vulnerability or self-exposure; reluctance to appear embarrassed reduces the story's interest and audience empathy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working Rubric: audience leaves having laughed and felt something
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the audience leave having laughed AND felt something?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the overall emotional impact: the best bits pair laughter with emotional resonance or insight rather than aiming for laughs alone.
